title: The GDScript debugger lost the ability to Pause infinite loops showing call stack in` _ready`
body:
### Tested versions

Started breaking somewhere between 4.2.2 and 4.3 (debugger no longer shows a breakpoint but an engine error is printed with a script stack), then somewhere between 4.5.1 and 4.6.2 it no longer prints at all.

### System information

Windows 11 64 bits

### Issue description

I have a GDScript infinite loop in my project, that occurs somewhere deep inside a `_ready` function. I thought I would be able to find it by simply pausing the project, but it doesn't work anymore.

In Godot 4.0, if you write an infinite loop inside `_ready`, pausing the game shows the GDScript debugger with the call stack where the script is executing, and you can see what the script is doing.

In Godot 4.6.2, you can also do that with an infinite loop occurring inside `_process`.
However, it no longer works in `_ready`.

I tried a bunch of Godot version:

Godot 4.0.4: it works

Godot 4.2.2: it works

Godot 4.3: doesn't work, and prints an error in the debugger's Errors tab:
```
E 0:00:01:0547   main.gd:16 @ _infinite_loop(): Parameter "script_lang" is null.
  <C++ Source>   core/debugger/remote_debugger.cpp:419 @ debug()
  <Stack Trace>  main.gd:16 @ _infinite_loop()
                 main.gd:5 @ _ready()
```

Godot 4.4: doesn't work either, and the same error prints.
Also, in this version there is the new "game embedding window", which has a "Pause" button too. But pressing that button doesn't work because the window is frozen. But curiously, after pressing it, the editor becomes frozen too.

Godot 4.5.1: doesn't work, same error prints.

Godot 4.6.2: doesn't work, and now the error no longer prints.
Also the editor still freezes eventually if the game window is interacted in any way.
**That means if you fall into that case and you use "Embed game on next play" (which is on by default), you will have to kill it and loose any unsaved changes in the editor.**



### Steps to reproduce

New project, one main scene with a `main.gd` script:
```gdscript
extends Node

func _ready() -> void:
	_infinite_loop()

func _infinite_loop() -> void:
	var x := 0
	while true:
		x += 1
		x += 1
		x -= 1
		x -= 1
```
Launch scene. Press the Pause button *in the editor*: observe it pauses, but doesn't show a call stack or anything helping see what the script is doing.

But if you change `_ready` to `_process`, it works fine.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[InfiniteLoop.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27412297/InfiniteLoop.zip)

Note: might be useful for people looking for ways to debug infinite loops https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/701
